searchText: sounds good to me! `bal-devnet-2` update from ACDT is to implement these 4 EIPs on top of block-level access lists: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/1460290791695188292. Putting it here for greater visibility. qq: in the spec it says that "Addresses accessed without state changes" must be included in the BAL, but does this mean they should be included even if they fail to warm the address in question? E.g. suppose you call `BALANCE 0xAA` with 100 gas (enough for warm case) and it fails OOG because you don't have enough for cold call - is `0xAA` added to BAL? Can anyone please tell me how to view full logs of a client in the bal-devnet-1? If they fail to warm up the address it should generally not be included afaik Are you part of a client team? It is not added to BAL in this case makes sense to me. should probably be made clearer in the spec though, because it right now it only explicitly says that this is the behavior for call operations Not really..just wanted to look at reth logs Agreed. I think this could even be a section in the EIP that explicitly states, for each affected instruction, what the gas boundary is for access. Also the order matters, one client could check memory expansion first and another could try to warm the account first and both fail but one may include the address in the BAL and the other won't. It seems like it is called out in the spec, but IMO it isn't very clear because then it finishes "if gas shortage causes the operation to fail before state access, the target address MUST NOT be included.". What if the client does the state access immediately upon warming the account? It would then conflict with the "only include if gas checks pass" and "if gas shortage causes op to fail" you can setup your own node and join the network <https://ethpandaops.io/networks/bal-devnet-1/>, but reth is currently debugging some syncing issues This is good for you to point out because we've all agreed on the implementation details here in the last month or so, but having someone with fresh eyes on the EIP that does not see this being clear in the spec reveals there is definitely room for refinement in the spec. i figured it had been discussed and decided 🙂 Yeah we've iterated across the gas boundaries for these cases, created tests, and aligned on implementation I think the spec could use some organization now, with the clearer instructions
